page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top. Quotation marks („) run down the right margin beside the text. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: Ut enim ( inquit Brutus, Philiatrum allo-quens ) dubitare non posfis aurum, argentum, ferrum, metallaque omnia: item unionem, hyacinthū, smaragdum, universumq; lapidum, concharumq; genus non ex uno, sed ex permistis quatuor illis rerum inijs originem duxisse. Et paulò ante oftenderat permistionem esse corporum & temperamentum solarum qualitatum. Eodem quoq; capite primi libri de Abditis, subiungic hęc, nempe concretis mistisq; corporibus gignendis, unius elementi materiam satis esse non posse, sed necesse esse, ut quatuor illa permistione confusa gignendis rebus idoneum subiectum exhibeant, substernantq;:Hæc Fernelius. Quibus clarissimè patet non solùm elementorum quali-tates, sed & eorum substantias permisceri mutarique, ut ex iis unio, continuatioque corporum, quæ ex his gignuntur, fieri possit.

page.notes: Printed quotation marks („) in the right margin beside each line are ornaments or ditto marks, not text, so they are not transcribed. A small printer's mark or reference symbol stands after "allo-" in the first line; it is unclear whether it is a note mark or an ornament, so it is not transcribed. Page number printed "2ʒ" (long-s form of 23), given as 23. The text has no headings. Several words are doubtful: "subiungic" is hyphenated across the line as printed "fubiun-gic"; "hęc" is read as printed but the letter may be "hæc" [?]; "universumq;" from printed "uniuerfumq;"; "substernantq;" from "fternantq;" with the mark before "Hæc" read as a colon. Printed spelling is preserved, including "posfis", "tum", "miftisq;" and the mixed s forms, with long s written as plain s.
